outline.description: Introduce the motivation for extending LSTMs in the era of Transformers and SSMs, summarize the paper’s central question, contributions, and high-level results.
subtopics: From LSTM success to Transformer dominance: context and challenges
Core question: Can scaled and improved LSTMs compete with modern LLMs?
Key contributions: exponential gating, new memory structures (sLSTM, mLSTM), xLSTM blocks and architectures
High-level findings: competitive perplexity, favorable scaling, strong long-context behavior
Roadmap of the textbook

outline.chapter_title: LSTM Foundations: Constant Error Carousel and Gating
outline.description: Provide a pedagogical refresher on LSTM mechanics, including the constant error carousel, gating, and standard formulations needed to understand xLSTM.

outline.description: Explain the three principal limitations that motivate xLSTM: revision of storage decisions, storage capacity, and parallelizability.

Sequential processing due to memory mixing: lack of parallelization
How these gaps led to Transformer adoption at scale
Design goals for xLSTM to address these limitations

outline.description: Introduce exponential gates, why they help with revisability, and the stabilization and normalization techniques that make them practical.

Practical activation and normalization choices

Covariance update rule: C_t = f_t C_{t-1} + i_t v_t k_t^T
Gate semantics: decay (forget), learning rate (input), output scaling
Normalizer vector n_t and denominator clamping for stability
Layer-norm assumptions, key scaling (1/sqrt(d))
Multiple cells vs. heads equivalence (no mixing)
Parallel formulation of the recurrence (scan/Flash-like)
Relation to Fast Weight Programmers and Retention

outline.chapter_title: Empirical Study I: Synthetic Tasks and Long Range Arena
outline.description: Assess xLSTM capabilities on formal languages (state tracking), multi-query associative recall (memory capacity), and LRA (long context).
subtopics: Formal languages suite and multi-length training for extrapolation
Finding: sLSTM enables state tracking tasks (e.g., parity) beyond SSMs/Transformers
Associative Recall with up to 256 pairs and context 2048
Finding: xLSTM[1:1] best among non-Transformers; sLSTM augments capacity
Extrapolation of memory capacity to longer contexts
Long Range Arena results: consistent strong long-context performance
Takeaways: revisability, capacity, and sequence-length robustness

outline.chapter_title: Empirical Study II: 15B-Token Language Modeling and Ablations
outline.description: Compare xLSTM to leading methods under matched settings and dissect contributions via ablations.
subtopics: Setup: SlimPajama 15B tokens, GPT-3-scale 350M parameter match
Baselines: Transformers (GPT-3, Llama), SSMs (H3, Mamba), RNNs/linear (RWKV, GLA, HGRN/HGRN2, RetNet, Hyena)
Main result: xLSTM achieves best validation perplexity
Scaling behavior at this scale indicates favorable trends
Ablation path: vanilla LSTM → residual backbone → post up-projection → exponential gates → matrix memory
Gate ablations: importance of learnable, input-dependent gates
Backbone component studies

outline.chapter_title: Empirical Study III: xLSTM as a Large Language Model (300B Tokens)
outline.description: Evaluate xLSTM at LLM scale: length extrapolation, validation perplexity, downstream tasks, PALOMA domains, scaling laws, and inference speed.
subtopics: Setup: SlimPajama 300B tokens; sizes 125M–1.3B; baselines Llama, Mamba, RWKV-4
Length extrapolation from 2k to 16k contexts: xLSTM maintains low perplexity
Validation perplexity across sizes: xLSTM[1:0] and [7:1] best overall
Downstream common-sense tasks: xLSTM leads broadly; ARC exceptions for Mamba
PALOMA across 571 domains: xLSTM[1:0] wins in vast majority of domains
Scaling laws: consistent power-law; xLSTM has best offset, promising larger-scale gains
Generation time and throughput: linear scaling; high-batch constant-memory advantage over Transformers
